sample_unit: diagnoses (topics) for which patient education materials were generated per LLM

links.outcome: Reading grade level of LLM-generated patient education materials versus 6th-grade target
links.effect: Initial outputs averaged grade 10.8 (ChatGPT), 12.2 (Copilot), 13.2 (Llama); all exceeded the recommended 6th-grade level; AAO averaged 8.0 FKGL.
links.quote: For all 15 topics, ChatGPT, Copilot, and Llama successfully generated PEMs, though all exceeded the recommended 6th-grade reading level.

links.outcome: Readability change after follow-up prompt to rewrite at 6th-grade level
links.effect: FRO prompting improved readability to 8.3 (ChatGPT), 11.2 (Copilot), 9.3 (Llama) (p<0.001), but still above 6th grade and not statistically easier than AAO (8.0).
links.quote: While initially prompted ChatGPT, Copilot, and Llama outputs were 10.8, 12.2, and 13.2, respectively, FRO prompting significantly improved readability to 8.3 for ChatGPT, 11.2 for Copilot, and 9.3 for Llama (p < 0.001).

unlisted_practices: Follow-up readability-optimized prompting of LLMs to reword patient education materials at a 6th-grade level

screen.practice: reading-level constraint via follow-up readability-optimized prompt
screen.reason: The study tests whether a follow-up readability-optimized (FRO) prompt constraint effectively reduces the reading grade level of LLM-generated patient education materials compared to baseline unconstrained prompting.
